Formulation:
Predisposing: Family history of autoimmune disease (heightened health vigilance); high work demands  
Precipitating: Onset of neurological symptoms (arm numbness, transient visual loss) and urgent discussion of possible serious diagnosis

Protective: Active help-seeking, supportive friends/co-workers, generally healthy lifestyle

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Health-related anxiety surrounding neurological symptoms
- Patient Goal(s): • Understand diagnostic process • Manage worry while awaiting specialist review • Maintain daily functioning (work, exercise, piano)
- Clinical Goal(s): • Reduce anxiety severity • Enhance coping strategies • Prevent escalation to generalized anxiety disorder
- Actions (Patient): • Practice scheduled worry time and relaxation exercises daily • Limit health-related internet searches to agreed sources • Maintain regular routine (sleep, balanced activity) • Record anxiety triggers/symptoms in journal
- Actions (Clinician/GP): • Provide clear information about referral timelines and what to expect • Offer brief CBT-based self-help materials for health anxiety • Arrange follow-up telehealth in 2 weeks to monitor mood/anxiety • Consider referral to psychologist if anxiety persists or escalates

Secondary Problem: Not recorded

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Nature of anxiety, linkage with uncertain health conditions, basic CBT techniques, when to seek urgent care (neurological red flags)
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Persistent rumination, sleep disturbance, avoidance of activities, panic symptoms
- Coping Strategies: Diaphragmatic breathing, progressive muscle relaxation, journaling, scheduled pleasurable activities, seeking social support

Consent, Coordination & Review:

- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: To be emailed post-consult (not yet sent)
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently

- Generalized Anxiety Disorder – Likelihood: Low. Justification: Worry present but not yet pervasive or longstanding enough for full GAD criteria.
